title: Adobe Illustrator MCP interface — preliminary reconstructed compatibility specification

tools.name: AlignObjects
tools.description: Aligns one or more objects along a specified edge or center axis. Objects can be aligned relative to each other (selection bounding box) or to the active artboard. Alignment is single-axis: 'left'/'center'/'right' shift X only (Y unchanged); 'top'/'middle'/'bottom' shift Y only (X unchanged). Prefer this tool over manual MoveObjects calculations whenever you need to align edges or centers of multiple objects.

parameters.name: uuids
parameters.description: Array of UUIDs of objects to align (minimum 1 when aligning to artboard, minimum 2 when aligning to selection). Layer UUIDs are not supported. IMPORTANT: pass as a native JSON array, not a stringified array.

parameters.name: alignment
parameters.description: Alignment axis: 'left', 'center', 'right', 'top', 'middle', or 'bottom'.

parameters.name: relativeTo
parameters.description: Reference frame: 'selection' (bounding box of all objects) or 'artboard' (active artboard bounds).

tools.name: DistributeObjects
tools.description: ALWAYS use this tool instead of manual MoveObjects offset math to CREATE or ADJUST equal gaps between 2+ objects \u2014 including improving/fixing/adjusting uniform tracking or letter-spacing in a wordmark/logotype/word made of separate letter objects. Not for pure repositioning of an already-spaced group (use MoveObjects instead, which preserves existing spacing). Only supports one uniform gap value for all objects, not unequal/proportional/ratio-based spacing (e.g. non-uniform kerning between specific letter pairs). Distributes objects evenly along an axis. If spacing is provided, objects are placed with that exact gap between them (2+ objects). If spacing is omitted, objects are distributed evenly within the total span from first to last (3+ objects required \u2014 pass explicit spacing instead for exactly 2 objects).

parameters.name: uuids
parameters.description: Array of UUIDs of objects to distribute (minimum 3 for even distribution, 2 for explicit spacing). Layer UUIDs are not supported. IMPORTANT: pass as a native JSON array, not a stringified array.

parameters.name: axis
parameters.description: Distribution axis: 'horizontal' or 'vertical'.

parameters.name: spacing
parameters.description: Explicit gap in points between objects. Omit to distribute evenly within current span.

tools.name: SetAppearance
tools.description: Sets visual appearance and state properties (fill, stroke, opacity, blend mode, locked, hidden, overprint) on one or more objects in a single call. All properties are optional \u2014 only provided properties are changed. To remove fill or stroke, set fillColor='none' or strokeColor='none'. Supports batch operations via uuids array. fillColor/strokeColor overwrite the entire fill/stroke of the objects you name with one literal color, applied exactly \u2014 use this tool whenever the request names a literal target color or color space, e.g. a hex, a Pantone/spot name, 'all red', or 'grayscale'/'black and white', at any scope from one object to a whole illustration ('make this illustration blue'). For 'grayscale'/'black and white' on multi-colored artwork, don't apply one flat gray to everything (that flattens the tonal variation) \u2014 read each object's current color via GetVisualAppearance, derive a gray from its luminance, and call once per distinct gray with the matching uuids. For an open-ended palette/theme/mood change with no fixed target color ('make it warmer', 'recolor to autumn', 'reduce to 2 colors'), use RecolorArtwork instead. NOTE: This tool handles flat colors only. For gradient fills or strokes \u2014 or to change angle, stops, or type on an existing gradient \u2014 use SetGradient instead. Providing a flat fillColor on an object with a gradient fill will replace the gradient with a flat color. Never invent, guess, or autocomplete swatch names. Text frames: fill/stroke color, paint toggles, overprint, and stroke-style properties apply to characters via the text engine; opacity and blend mode behavior is unchanged. IMPORTANT: Set locked=false or hidden=false ONLY when the user explicitly asks to unlock/show objects or explicitly references locked/hidden state (e.g., 'unlock layer X', 'show the hidden group', 'delete the locked layer'). Generic requests like 'delete all', 'move everything', 'rotate the shapes', or 'place/add X in layer Y' do NOT grant permission to unlock/unhide first, even if that's the only way to fulfill the request \u2014 ask the user instead. When a requested fill/stroke/paint change can't be applied to an object's type, that object is reported in skipped_objects (with skipped_count and a per-object reason), NOT failed_objects; opacity, blend mode, locked, and hidden still apply. Symbol instances are the common case \u2014 the response additionally carries a symbol_link_guidance field explaining the symbol link must be broken first. Response shape: {success, details, success_count, fail_count, failed_objects?, skipped_count, skipped_objects?, symbol_link_guidance?}.

parameters.name: uuids
parameters.description: UUIDs of objects to style. Always pass an array, even for one object.

parameters.name: fillColor
parameters.description: Fill color. Hex '#RRGGBB', a named document swatch via {\\\"model\\\":\\\"swatch\\\",\\\"name\\\":\\\"PANTONE 485 C\\\"}, or a color object (for example {\\\"model\\\":\\\"cmyk\\\",\\\"c\\\":0.15,\\\"m\\\":0.7,\\\"y\\\":0.35,\\\"k\\\":0.05}). Use 'none' to remove fill. Omit for no change. For object models rgb/cmyk/gray, prefer normalized channels in [0,1] (for example {\\\"model\\\":\\\"rgb\\\",\\\"r\\\":0.25,\\\"g\\\":0.4,\\\"b\\\":0.9}, {\\\"model\\\":\\\"cmyk\\\",\\\"c\\\":0.15,\\\"m\\\":0.7,\\\"y\\\":0.35,\\\"k\\\":0.05}, or {\\\"model\\\":\\\"gray\\\",\\\"gray\\\":0.5}); if your RGB source values are 0-255 bytes, prefer hex '#RRGGBB'. Accepts: hex like '#RRGGBB' or '#RGB' (sugar), 'none' to remove, or an object: {\"model\":\"rgb\",\"r\":1,\"g\":0,\"b\":0} | {\"model\":\"cmyk\",\"c\":0,\"m\":1,\"y\":1,\"k\":0} | {\"model\":\"gray\",\"gray\":0.5} | {\"model\":\"swatch\",\"name\":\"PANTONE 185 C\",\"tint\":0.5}.

parameters.name: strokeColor
parameters.description: Stroke color. Hex '#RRGGBB', a named document swatch via {\\\"model\\\":\\\"swatch\\\",\\\"name\\\":\\\"PANTONE 485 C\\\"}, or a color object (for example {\\\"model\\\":\\\"cmyk\\\",\\\"c\\\":0.15,\\\"m\\\":0.7,\\\"y\\\":0.35,\\\"k\\\":0.05}). Use 'none' to remove stroke. Omit for no change. For object models rgb/cmyk/gray, prefer normalized channels in [0,1] (for example {\\\"model\\\":\\\"rgb\\\",\\\"r\\\":0.25,\\\"g\\\":0.4,\\\"b\\\":0.9}, {\\\"model\\\":\\\"cmyk\\\",\\\"c\\\":0.15,\\\"m\\\":0.7,\\\"y\\\":0.35,\\\"k\\\":0.05}, or {\\\"model\\\":\\\"gray\\\",\\\"gray\\\":0.5}); if your RGB source values are 0-255 bytes, prefer hex '#RRGGBB'. ONLY pass a color when the user explicitly names one; otherwise omit so the tool uses the Color panel's current stroke swatch \u2014 do NOT default to black. Accepts: hex like '#RRGGBB' or '#RGB' (sugar), 'none' to remove, or an object: {\"model\":\"rgb\",\"r\":1,\"g\":0,\"b\":0} | {\"model\":\"cmyk\",\"c\":0,\"m\":1,\"y\":1,\"k\":0} | {\"model\":\"gray\",\"gray\":0.5} | {\"model\":\"swatch\",\"name\":\"PANTONE 185 C\",\"tint\":0.5}.

parameters.name: strokeWeight
parameters.description: Absolute stroke width in points. Omit for no change. Use strokeWeightDelta for relative changes ('increase'/'decrease') \u2014 never guess the current value.

parameters.name: strokeWeightDelta
parameters.description: Relative stroke width change in points (positive=thicker, negative=thinner). Reads the live current weight and adds this delta, clamped to [0,1000]. Use instead of strokeWeight when the user says 'increase', 'decrease', 'thicker', 'thinner'.

parameters.name: strokeCap
parameters.description: Line cap style. Omit to leave unchanged.

parameters.name: strokeJoin
parameters.description: Line join style. Omit to leave unchanged.

parameters.name: strokeDash
parameters.description: Dash pattern as array of numbers (e.g. [12,4,2,4]). Omit for no change. [] = solid line.

parameters.name: opacity
parameters.description: Opacity 0-1 (0=transparent, 1=opaque). Omit for no change.

parameters.name: blendMode
parameters.description: Blend mode. Omit to leave unchanged.

parameters.name: locked
parameters.description: Lock state: true = lock, false = unlock. Omit for no change. WARNING: Never unlock unless the user's request explicitly mentions locked state. Ask the user first if unsure.

parameters.name: hidden
parameters.description: Visibility: true = hide, false = show. Omit for no change. WARNING: Never unhide unless the user's request explicitly mentions hidden state. Ask the user first if unsure.

parameters.name: overprintFill
parameters.description: Overprint fill: true = overprint, false = no overprint. Primarily meaningful for CMYK/spot-color print workflows. Omit for no change.

parameters.name: overprintStroke
parameters.description: Overprint stroke: true = overprint, false = no overprint. Primarily meaningful for CMYK/spot-color print workflows. Omit for no change.

tools.name: ListArtboards
tools.description: Get details of all artboards including name, locked state, bounds, and valid canvas bounds. Coordinates are canvas-global in points with Y-down. Returns artboards[] (the list to iterate) and canvas_bounds ([left,top,right,bottom]).

tools.name: CreateArtboard
tools.description: Add a new artboard to the current document. This is the default way to get a new canvas at a different size (book cover, poster, social variant, print format) \u2014 an Illustrator document can hold many artboards at different sizes, so new-size requests rarely need CreateDocument. left/top omitted \u2192 auto-positions right of the last artboard with a 20pt gap, wrapping to a new row if needed. Coordinates canvas-global, points, Y-down. Must stay within the canvas \u2014 see ListArtboards' canvas_bounds. Requires a document open.

parameters.name: left
parameters.description: Left (X) in points. Must be within canvas_bounds returned by ListArtboards. Omit to auto-position to the right of the last artboard.

parameters.name: top
parameters.description: Top (Y) in points. Must be within canvas_bounds returned by ListArtboards. Omit to auto-position.

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: Width in points

parameters.name: height
parameters.description: Height in points

parameters.name: artboardName
parameters.description: Name for the artboard (auto-generated if empty)

parameters.name: backgroundColor
parameters.description: Artboard background color. Use 'none' to leave the artboard transparent. Omit to inherit the document/preference default. Only rgb, cmyk, or 'none' are accepted by AIArtboardSuite \u2014 gray and named swatches are rejected. Accepts: hex like '#RRGGBB' or '#RGB' (sugar), 'none' to remove, or an object: {\"model\":\"rgb\",\"r\":1,\"g\":0,\"b\":0} | {\"model\":\"cmyk\",\"c\":0,\"m\":1,\"y\":1,\"k\":0} | {\"model\":\"gray\",\"gray\":0.5}.

tools.name: SetArtboardProperties
tools.description: Sets one or more properties of an artboard atomically in a single update. Resolves the target artboard by artboardIndex, then artboardName, then falls back to the active artboard. newName: rename the artboard. backgroundColor: hex ('#RRGGBB' / '#RGB') or structured color objects (rgb / cmyk); 'none' clears the background. Named swatches are not supported. presetName: resize to a named preset (e.g. 'A4', 'iPhone X', 'Instagram Story', 'HDV/HDTV 720'). Always use this for ANY request that names a device, paper size, social-media format, or video standard \u2014 even if you know the canonical pixel/point dimensions. Never guess a presetName \u2014 call GetArtboardProperties with no arguments first to see every valid name, then pass an exact match. When presetName is used, orientation is auto-detected from the artboard's current width/height so the existing orientation is always preserved by default. Only pass orientation when the user explicitly asks to change it. At least one property must be provided. Prefer this tool over sequential single-property calls when changing multiple properties at once. Resulting artboard bounds must stay within the canvas \u2014 see ListArtboards' canvas_bounds.

parameters.name: artboardIndex
parameters.description: 1-based artboard index from ListArtboards (1 = first artboard). Omit to use artboardName or active artboard.

parameters.name: artboardName
parameters.description: Name of the artboard to update (empty to use index or active)

parameters.name: newName
parameters.description: New name for the artboard (omit to leave unchanged)

parameters.name: presetName
parameters.description: Named preset to apply (e.g. 'A4', 'Instagram Story', 'HDV/HDTV 720'). Case-insensitive. Dimensions are applied according to orientation (auto-detected from current artboard when omitted). Omit to leave dimensions unchanged.

parameters.name: orientation
parameters.description: Desired orientation for the preset. 'landscape': longer preset dim becomes width. 'portrait': longer preset dim becomes height. 'square': applies the preset's raw dim1/dim2 values as-is without any reordering (only meaningful for genuinely square presets). Omit to auto-detect from the artboard's current width/height (square artboards default to portrait). Only provide when the user explicitly asks to change orientation.

parameters.name: backgroundColor
parameters.description: Background color. Use 'none' to clear the background color. Omit to leave unchanged. Only rgb, cmyk, or 'none' are accepted by AIArtboardSuite \u2014 gray and named swatches are rejected. Accepts: hex like '#RRGGBB' or '#RGB' (sugar), 'none' to remove, or an object: {\"model\":\"rgb\",\"r\":1,\"g\":0,\"b\":0} | {\"model\":\"cmyk\",\"c\":0,\"m\":1,\"y\":1,\"k\":0} | {\"model\":\"gray\",\"gray\":0.5}.

tools.name: DuplicateArtboard
tools.description: Duplicate an existing artboard to newLeft/newTop with an optional new name (auto-generated if empty). Coordinates are canvas-global points, Y-down. When duplicateContent is true the artwork moves with the artboard by the same offset; if the requested position would make the copy overlap the source, it is automatically placed at a non-overlapping position clear of the source and the final coordinates are reported in the response \u2014 unless no room remains within the canvas, in which case the call fails with an actionable error. Must stay within the canvas \u2014 see ListArtboards' canvas_bounds.

parameters.name: artboardIndex
parameters.description: 1-based artboard index from ListArtboards (1 = first artboard). Omit to use artboardName or active artboard.

parameters.name: artboardName
parameters.description: Name of the artboard to duplicate (empty to use index or active)

parameters.name: newName
parameters.description: Name for the duplicated artboard (auto-generated if empty)

parameters.name: newLeft
parameters.description: Left (X) of the new artboard in points. Must be within canvas_bounds returned by ListArtboards.

parameters.name: newTop
parameters.description: Top (Y) of the new artboard in points. Must be within canvas_bounds returned by ListArtboards.

parameters.name: duplicateContent
parameters.description: Also duplicate artwork on the artboard (default: true)

tools.name: GetActiveArtboard
tools.description: Get details of the currently active artboard. Result: artboards[0] contains index, name, locked, bounds [left,top,right,bottom] in Y-down points. Derive width = right - left, height = bottom - top for proportional positioning (e.g. center x = left + width * 0.5, lower-third y = top + height * 0.65).

tools.name: ScaleArtboards
tools.description: Scale or resize artboards. Do NOT use this tool for named preset requests like 'iPhone X', 'A4', 'Instagram Story', 'HDV/HDTV 720' \u2014 call GetArtboardProperties to look up dim1_pt/dim2_pt, decide which to use as width/height based on the artboard's current orientation or user request, then call SetArtboardProperties with presetName or use this tool with mode='absolute' and the chosen dimensions. The 'mode' parameter controls how scaleXValues/scaleYValues are interpreted:   mode='factor': values are multipliers (1.0=no change, 2.0=double, 0.5=halve).   mode='absolute': values are target width/height in points (e.g. 500 means 500pt). Prefer mode='absolute' when the user gives exact dimensions (e.g. '500 by 700 points'). Scaling is applied around per-artboard anchor points (defaults to 'center'). Valid anchors (hyphenated): 'top-left','top-center','top-right','center-left','center','center-right','bottom-left','bottom-center','bottom-right'. Use anchors to pin a specific corner or edge during resize, e.g. anchors=['bottom-right'] keeps the bottom-right corner fixed while the artboard grows/shrinks from the top-left. Artwork scales with the artboard by default (scaleContent=true); set scaleContent=false to resize the artboard only. When scaleContent=true, artwork preserves its own aspect ratio by default (maintainAspectRatioOfContent) even when the artboard itself is resized non-uniformly - see maintainAspectRatioOfContent. All provided arrays must match the length of artboardIndices. Locked artboards are skipped unless force=true. Must stay within the canvas \u2014 see ListArtboards' canvas_bounds.

parameters.name: artboardIndices
parameters.description: 1-based artboard indices to scale (1 = first artboard).

parameters.name: scaleXValues
parameters.description: mode='factor': horizontal multiplier per artboard. mode='absolute': target width in points per artboard.

parameters.name: scaleYValues
parameters.description: mode='factor': vertical multiplier per artboard. mode='absolute': target height in points per artboard.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Required. 'factor': scaleXValues/scaleYValues are multipliers. 'absolute': they are target dimensions in points.

parameters.name: anchors
parameters.description: Per-artboard anchor point for scaling origin. Each element must be one of: 'top-left','top-center','top-right','center-left','center','center-right','bottom-left','bottom-center','bottom-right'. Defaults to 'center' for all artboards when omitted.

parameters.name: scaleContent
parameters.description: Scale artwork inside each artboard along with it. Set false to resize artboard only without scaling artwork.

parameters.name: maintainAspectRatioOfContent
parameters.description: Default true. Only affects how artwork is scaled when scaleContent=true - the artboard itself always resizes exactly to scaleXValues[i]/scaleYValues[i], independently per axis, regardless of this setting. When true, artwork is always scaled uniformly to fit within the new artboard size without exceeding either dimension (preserving proportions), and is normally also centered in the new artboard on any axis with leftover space - centering is skipped (aspect ratio is still preserved) only in the rare case content bounds cannot be read. Set to false ONLY when the user explicitly says stretching/squashing/distorting the artwork is acceptable (e.g. 'it's fine if the content stretches', 'squeeze it to fit exactly', 'don't worry about distortion') - this stretches/squashes artwork to exactly match the new artboard dimensions, same as the artboard itself. Otherwise keep the default true.

parameters.name: force
parameters.description: Set true only when user explicitly asks to scale locked artboards.

tools.name: FitArtboard
tools.description: Resize an artboard's bounds to tightly enclose artwork \u2014 does NOT change the viewport or zoom level. The 'scope' parameter controls which artwork is considered: 'artboard' (default) fits to any artwork whose bounds intersect the target artboard, even partially; 'all' fits to all artwork in the document; 'selected' fits to currently selected objects; 'objects' fits to specific objects by UUID (requires uuids parameter). Prefer 'objects' when you have UUIDs; use 'selected' only when the user explicitly refers to their current selection. Reports new bounds in details. Note: this tool resizes the artboard itself, not the view. There is no MCP tool for zoom/pan \u2014 those are view-only actions handled by the app's View menu. Locked artboards are protected by default and cannot be fit unless force=true. Resulting artboard bounds must stay within the canvas \u2014 see ListArtboards' canvas_bounds.

parameters.name: artboardIndex
parameters.description: 1-based artboard index from ListArtboards (1 = first artboard). Omit to use artboardName or active artboard.

parameters.name: artboardName
parameters.description: Name of the artboard (empty to use index or active)

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Which artwork to fit: 'artboard' (overlapping target artboard, default), 'all' (all artwork in document), 'selected' (currently selected objects \u2014 fails if nothing is selected), 'objects' (specific UUIDs \u2014 must also provide uuids parameter).

parameters.name: uuids
parameters.description: UUIDs of objects to fit to. Required when scope='objects'. Always pass an array, even for one object.

parameters.name: force
parameters.description: Default false. Set to true only when the user explicitly asks to fit a locked artboard. General requests like 'fit all artboards except locked ones' must leave this false.

tools.name: DeleteArtboard
tools.description: Remove an artboard from the document. By default the artwork on the artboard is preserved; set removeContent=true ONLY when the user explicitly asks to delete the artwork too. Returns the updated artboard list with new indices after deletion. This tool deletes artboards only, not layers. artboardName must be an artboard name from ListArtboards. removeContent only controls whether artwork on the deleted artboard is also removed; it does not delete layers by name. Locked artboards are protected by default and cannot be deleted unless force=true. Set force=true only when the user explicitly asks to delete a locked artboard. To delete individual objects or layers without removing the artboard, use DeleteObjects instead. Cannot remove the last artboard \u2014 a document must have at least one artboard. If only one artboard exists and you need different dimensions, position, or name, use ScaleArtboards, MoveArtboards, or SetArtboardProperties instead.

parameters.name: artboardIndex
parameters.description: 1-based artboard index from ListArtboards (1 = first artboard). Omit to use artboardName or active artboard.

parameters.name: artboardName
parameters.description: Artboard name from ListArtboards (not a layer name; empty to use index or active)

parameters.name: removeContent
parameters.description: Default false. Set to true only when the user explicitly asks to also delete the artwork on the artboard (e.g. 'delete the artboard and its contents'). Generic requests like 'delete the artboard' or 'remove artboard 2' must leave this false \u2014 the artboard is removed but its artwork is preserved.

parameters.name: force
parameters.description: Default false. Set to true only when the user explicitly asks to delete a locked artboard. General requests like 'delete all artboards except locked ones' must leave this false.

tools.name: SetActiveArtboard
tools.description: Set a specific artboard as active and selected. Locked or hidden artboards become active but may not be selected.

parameters.name: artboardIndex
parameters.description: 1-based artboard index from ListArtboards (1 = first artboard). Omit to use artboardName or active artboard.

parameters.name: artboardName
parameters.description: Name of the artboard to set as active (empty to use index)

tools.name: MoveArtboards
tools.description: Reposition multiple artboards in a single batch operation. Artwork on each artboard moves with it by default (moveContent=true). This tool snapshots art-to-artboard associations before any moves, so artboards can safely swap positions or overlap during rearrangement without stealing each other's content, as long as every affected artboard's move is included in this same call \u2014 never split one interdependent rearrangement across multiple calls. All three arrays must have the same length. Coordinates are canvas-global in points with Y-down. Must stay within the canvas \u2014 see ListArtboards' canvas_bounds. Locked artboards are skipped unless force=true. NOTE: Artboard frames are committed before art transforms; transforming art may partially fail, so the result may include successfully moved artboards with partially transformed content.

parameters.name: artboardIndices
parameters.description: 1-based artboard indices to move (1 = first artboard). Must match lengths of newLefts and newTops.

parameters.name: newLefts
parameters.description: New left (X) position for each artboard in points.

parameters.name: newTops
parameters.description: New top (Y) position for each artboard in points (Y-down).

parameters.name: moveContent
parameters.description: Move artwork inside each artboard along with it (default: true).

parameters.name: force
parameters.description: Default false. Set true only when user explicitly asks to move locked artboards. General requests like 'rearrange all unlocked artboards' must leave this false.

tools.name: GetArtboardProperties
tools.description: Look up artboard presets available in Illustrator (Print, Web, Video, Social, Branding, Mobile). Each preset reports dim1_pt and dim2_pt \u2014 the raw values returned by the Illustrator preset table. Mobile preset dimensions are screen pixels (= points at Illustrator's 72-PPI screen baseline, matching the Artboard Properties panel). Pass presetName for an exact (case-insensitive) lookup of a single preset; omit to list all presets. Never guess a presetName \u2014 call with no arguments first to see every valid name, then pass an exact match. Pass category to filter by category when listing all.

parameters.name: presetName
parameters.description: Preset name for an exact case-insensitive lookup (e.g. 'A4', 'Instagram Story').

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Category filter when listing all presets. One of: 'Print', 'Web', 'Video', 'Social', 'Branding', 'Mobile'. Ignored when presetName is provided.

tools.name: GetCanvasStructure
tools.description: Browse the document's layer hierarchy. Returns objects_basic_details array with basic details per node: uuid, name, object_type, bounds (when present), child_count, child_types, locked (when true), hidden (when true) \u2014 both inherited from ancestors; is_generative (when true), generative_type (when present), has_edit_lineage (when true); and current_layer (when available) with the uuid and locked/hidden state of the document's active layer. Layers and children are in z-order (0=frontmost/top). Use this to explore layers and groups top-down. To get all objects on a specific artboard instead, use GetArtboardStructure. Use 'maxDepth' to control depth: -1 = unlimited (all descendants), 0 (default) = top-level only, 1 = immediate children, 2+ = deeper. Nodes at the depth limit show child_count/child_types summary instead of children. Omit 'uuids' to start from document layers. Pass 'uuids' to start from specific objects (groups, layers, etc.). For detailed properties (text_content, geometry), use GetObjectStructure. LARGE RESPONSES: Children are expanded breadth-first (all siblings at each depth before going deeper). When the response size limit is reached, expansion stops \u2014 groups already listed retain child_count/child_types summaries for navigation. Results include truncated=true and resume_hint. Call GetObjectStructure on specific group UUIDs to drill deeper.

parameters.name: uuids
parameters.description: Optional array of object UUIDs to use as starting points. Omit to start from document layers (default). Always pass an array, even for one object.

parameters.name: maxDepth
parameters.description: Depth of children to include. 0 = starting nodes only (default). 1 = starting nodes + immediate children. 2+ = deeper. -1 = unlimited (all descendants). Groups/layers at the depth limit show child_count and child_types summary instead of children.

tools.name: GetArtboardStructure
tools.description: Get all objects visually overlapping an artboard, regardless of which layer they belong to. Returns artboards (index, bounds) and objects_basic_details array in z-order (0=frontmost/top). To browse by layer hierarchy instead, use GetCanvasStructure. Each object includes uuid, name, object_type, bounds, is_selected, locked (when true), hidden (when true) \u2014 both inherited from ancestors; is_generative (when true), generative_type (when present), has_edit_lineage (when true); groups also have child_count and child_types. Groups are NOT recursively expanded \u2014 call GetObjectStructure on a group uuid to inspect contents. LARGE RESPONSES: When too many objects exist, partial results are returned with truncated=true and resume_hint with instructions on how to continue.

parameters.name: artboardIndex
parameters.description: 1-based artboard index from ListArtboards (1 = first artboard). Omit to use the active artboard.

tools.name: VisualizeSelection
tools.description: Get the selection roots (the objects the user actually selected, not descendants of an already-selected parent), in z-order (0=frontmost/top). Returns objects_basic_details array; each entry has uuid, name, object_type, bounds, locked (when true), hidden (when true) \u2014 both inherited from ancestors; is_generative (when true), generative_type (when present), has_edit_lineage (when true); groups also have child_count and child_types. To inspect a selected group's contents, call GetObjectStructure on its uuid. LARGE RESPONSES: When too many objects are selected, partial results are returned with truncated=true and resume_hint with instructions on how to continue.

tools.name: CreateDocument
tools.description: Create a new, separate Illustrator file. Most tasks do NOT need one \u2014 an Illustrator document holds many artboards at different sizes, and keeping variants (book cover, poster, social sizes, print formats) in one file lets the user compare and export them together. Use ONLY when the user explicitly asks for a new file, or the required colorMode/units/bleed differs from the current document. For a new canvas at a different size in the current document, use CreateArtboard. Returns the initial artboard's bounds and index in artboards.

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: Artboard width in the specified units (default: points)

parameters.name: height
parameters.description: Artboard height in the specified units (default: points)

parameters.name: documentName
parameters.description: Name for the new document

parameters.name: colorMode
parameters.description: Document color mode

parameters.name: rasterEffectsResolution
parameters.description: Raster effects resolution (affects live effects like drop shadows)

parameters.name: units
parameters.description: Document ruler units. Use short form 'mm' (not 'millimeters')

parameters.name: bleed
parameters.description: Document bleed in the specified units. Pass [value] for uniform bleed on all sides, or 4 per-side values [left, top, right, bottom]. Exactly 1 or 4 values accepted. All values must be >= 0.

parameters.name: artboardName
parameters.description: Name for the initial artboard

parameters.name: artboardBackgroundColor
parameters.description: Initial artboard background color. Use 'none' for no background. Omit to use the application default. Only rgb, cmyk, or 'none' are accepted by AIArtboardSuite \u2014 named swatches are rejected. Accepts: hex like '#RRGGBB' or '#RGB' (sugar), 'none' to remove, or an object: {\"model\":\"rgb\",\"r\":1,\"g\":0,\"b\":0} | {\"model\":\"cmyk\",\"c\":0,\"m\":1,\"y\":1,\"k\":0} | {\"model\":\"gray\",\"gray\":0.5}.

tools.name: OpenDocument
tools.description: Opens an existing file in Illustrator. Returns document metadata and artboard details so you can immediately start working. The previously active document remains open and can be switched back to with SwitchDocument.

parameters.name: filePath
parameters.description: Absolute path to the file to open (supports ~ for home directory). Must be provided by the user \u2014 never guess or fabricate file paths.

tools.name: ListDocuments
tools.description: Lists all open documents with metadata. The active document includes full details: colorMode, units, artboardCount, bleedInsets, rasterEffectsResolution, colorProfiles, width, height, document_profile (Print/Web/Video/Mobile), document_title (string, from XMP dc:title), and document_language (string, e.g. 'en-US', from XMP dc:language). Inactive documents include name, path, and index.

tools.name: SwitchDocument
tools.description: Switches the active document by index, name, or file path. Returns full document metadata and artboard details for the newly active document. Use ListDocuments first to see available documents. Provide exactly one of: index, name, or filePath.

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: Document index from ListDocuments (0-based). Omit to use name or filePath instead.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Document name to switch to

parameters.name: filePath
parameters.description: Document file path to switch to

tools.name: GetUndoStack
tools.description: Returns the undo/redo stack for the current document. Each entry includes its History-Panel label, internal tag, and an is_empty flag. Use is_empty == true to detect phantom undo entries caused by the parallel-document bug.

tools.name: ApplyEffect
tools.description: Applies a live effect to one or more objects. Supported effects: 'drop_shadow', 'gaussian_blur', 'extrude_3d'. Effect-specific parameters are optional: omitted parameters use sensible defaults when creating a new effect, and preserve existing values when updating an existing one (exception: extrude_3d requires extrudeDepth when creating a new effect). Never invent, guess, or autocomplete swatch names.

parameters.name: uuids
parameters.description: UUIDs of the objects to apply the effect to. Layer UUIDs are not supported. Always pass an array, even for one object.

parameters.name: effectType
parameters.description: Effect to apply

parameters.name: blurRadius
parameters.description: Blur radius in points (drop_shadow & gaussian_blur). Omit to preserve the existing value when updating an effect; defaults to 5 when creating a new one.

parameters.name: offsetX
parameters.description: Horizontal shadow offset in points (drop_shadow only, positive = right). Omit to preserve the existing value when updating an effect; defaults to 5 when creating a new one.

parameters.name: offsetY
parameters.description: Vertical shadow offset in points (drop_shadow only, positive = down). Omit to preserve the existing value when updating an effect; defaults to 5 when creating a new one.

parameters.name: opacity
parameters.description: Shadow opacity 0-1 (drop_shadow only). Omit to preserve the existing value when updating an effect; defaults to 0.75 when creating a new one.

parameters.name: colorHex
parameters.description: Shadow color when colorSource='color' (drop_shadow only). Accepts hex and other structured color forms supported by tool color input (e.g. CMYK, gray, swatch). Omit to preserve the existing color when updating an effect; defaults to opaque black when creating a new one. Drop shadow does not support 'none'. Accepts: hex like '#RRGGBB' or '#RGB' (sugar), or an object: {\"model\":\"rgb\",\"r\":1,\"g\":0,\"b\":0} | {\"model\":\"cmyk\",\"c\":0,\"m\":1,\"y\":1,\"k\":0} | {\"model\":\"gray\",\"gray\":0.5} | {\"model\":\"swatch\",\"name\":\"PANTONE 185 C\",\"tint\":0.5}. The 'none' sentinel is not accepted here.

parameters.name: colorSource
parameters.description: Shadow color source (drop_shadow only): 'color' uses colorHex, 'darkness' tints source artwork colors. Omit to preserve the existing mode when updating an effect; defaults to 'color' when creating a new one.

parameters.name: darkness
parameters.description: Darkness percentage 0-100 for source-color tinting (drop_shadow only, used when colorSource='darkness'). Omit to preserve the existing value when updating an effect; defaults to 100 when creating a new one.

parameters.name: extrudeDepth
parameters.description: Extrusion depth in points (extrude_3d only). Required when creating a new 3D effect. When updating an existing effect, omit to preserve the current value.

parameters.name: bevelStyle
parameters.description: Bevel edge style for 3D extrude (extrude_3d only): a bevel profile, or 'none' for a plain extrude (no bevel). When creating a new effect, omitting this produces a plain extrude. When updating an existing 3D extrude, omit to preserve the current bevel and pass 'none' to remove it.

parameters.name: rotation
parameters.description: 3D rotation as [x, y, z] in degrees (extrude_3d only). Provide all three axes. Omit to preserve the current view when updating an existing effect, or to use the default 3/4 view when creating a new one.

parameters.name: existingEffectBehavior
parameters.description: How to handle an existing same-type effect (drop_shadow / gaussian_blur only; IGNORED for extrude_3d, which always applies/updates the object's single 3D effect): 'auto' updates when exactly one matching existing effect is found, appends when none are found, and for multiple matches only applies bulk-safe updates that are unambiguous across all matches; otherwise it fails. Note: auto can also append when style parsing is unavailable (parser suite missing or style not parseable). 'modify_existing' updates only and fails if no safe unique target exists; 'append_new' always adds another effect entry.

tools.name: Export
tools.description: Exports artwork to a file, returns it as a stream, or uploads it to an Adobe-hosted URL. Supports raster formats (PNG, JPEG, TIFF, PSD, WEBP, BMP), vector formats (SVG, PDF, EPS, DWG, DXF), and native Illustrator format (AI). Target what to export: CANVAS (entire document, default), ARTBOARD (single artboard by index), UUID (specific objects by uuid \u2014 no selection needed), or SELECTION (currently selected objects). Output goes to one of three places: provide `outputPath` for file mode (default), `outputMode='stream'` for inline data (PNG/SVG only), or `uploadTo` for a direct upload to a presigned URL. For the presigned-upload flow: obtain uploadTo from the host's canvas-upload preparation step and pass it here exactly as given; leave authBearer unset \u2014 a presigned URL already carries its own signature, and adding a Bearer header breaks it. No `url` is returned in `details` for this path (it's a raw-byte PUT, not a harness POST); success just means the bytes are uploaded, and the caller resolves the final asset URL in a separate step. Never guess a value for uploadTo/authBearer yourself. For file mode, provide outputPath with a full path. Host OS comes only from client_platform on each prompt (macos|windows) \u2014 never infer OS from user path syntax. Passing a group or layer UUID exports all children within that container. Omit optional styling parameters (antiAlias, backgroundColor, quality, colorModel, etc.) unless the user explicitly asked for them \u2014 when omitted, the user's saved Export Preferences are used. Never guess their values. Do not use this tool for a Save or Save As request \u2014 exporting is not saving.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Export format. 'AI' is Adobe Illustrator native format (.ai). JPG is an alias for JPEG; TIF is an alias for TIFF. EPS hard-fails with an error if the document contains broken linked files; all other formats in file mode include a non-fatal warning in the response `warnings` array.

parameters.name: outputPath
parameters.description: Output file path. Required for file mode. Use client_platform on the prompt (macos|windows) for host OS when composing default paths \u2014 never infer OS from user path shape. User-given paths \u2192 verbatim; never silently remap (e.g. do not rewrite C:\\\\... to ~/...). If an explicit user path conflicts with client_platform, explain the mismatch and ask for a path valid on this host. `~` = user profile; use client_platform for separators when composing paths. Never use %VAR% tokens. Mac (client_platform=macos): ~, /Volumes/..., /Users/Shared, /tmp, /var/folders/..., ~/Library/CloudStorage, ~/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs; blocked: other ~/Library sub-paths, other users, OS dirs. Win (client_platform=windows): ~, D:\\\\, E:\\\\..., ~\\\\AppData\\\\Local\\\\Temp; blocked: ~\\\\AppData\\\\Roaming, ~\\\\AppData\\\\Local (except Temp), Program Files, ProgramData, C:\\\\Users\\\\Public, app folder, other users, OS dirs, UNC. Verify root before calling. No filename from the user? Omit the leaf \u2014 pass a folder path ending with / (e.g. ~/Desktop/<<DOC_NAME>>/); the tool fills the filename from the target's own name. Don't look the name up yourself. Mutually exclusive with uploadTo.

parameters.name: uploadTo
parameters.description: Presigned upload URL obtained from the host's canvas-upload preparation step \u2014 pass it exactly as given, never construct or guess one yourself. Only Adobe-owned hosts are accepted (*.adobe.io / *.adobe.com, or known Adobe S3 backends for the presigned flow). Mutually exclusive with outputPath. Leave authBearer unset for this flow (empty authBearer = raw-bytes PUT to a presigned URL, no `url` in the response). Non-empty authBearer instead selects the separate multipart-POST harness-upload contract (response's `url` returned in `details`) \u2014 do not mix the two.

parameters.name: authBearer
parameters.description: Leave unset for the presigned-upload flow (uploadTo from the host's canvas-upload preparation step) \u2014 a presigned URL already carries its own signature, and adding a Bearer header breaks it. Only set this for the separate multipart-POST harness-upload contract.

parameters.name: targetType
parameters.description: Target to export

parameters.name: outputMode
parameters.description: 'file' saves to the specified outputPath; 'stream' returns inline data (PNG/SVG only). Ignored when uploadTo is set.

parameters.name: uuids
parameters.description: UUIDs of objects, groups, or layers to export. Pass one or more UUIDs when targetType=UUID. Get UUIDs from GetCanvasStructure. Always pass an array, even for one object.

parameters.name: artboardIndex
parameters.description: 1-based artboard index from ListArtboards (1 = first artboard). Omit to use the active artboard.

parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description: DPI for raster exports (PNG, JPEG, PSD, WEBP, TIFF, BMP). Screen baseline is 72 DPI \u2014 use this to convert scale factors: 0.5x=36, 0.75x=54, 1x=72, 2x=144, 3x=216. Always pass this when the prompt specifies a scale factor or resolution.

parameters.name: quality
parameters.description: quality (JPEG: 0\u201310 where 5 is default; WebP: 0\u2013100).

parameters.name: antiAlias
parameters.description: Anti-aliasing. Applies to: PNG, JPEG, PSD, WebP, TIFF, BMP.

parameters.name: colorModel
parameters.description: Color model. Applies to: JPEG (RGB/CMYK/grayscale), PSD (RGB/CMYK/grayscale), TIFF (RGB/CMYK/grayscale), BMP (RGB/grayscale/bitmap).

parameters.name: embedColorProfile
parameters.description: Embed ICC color profile. Applies to: JPEG, WEBP, AI, PSD, TIFF. Not applicable to PDF.

parameters.name: backgroundColor
parameters.description: Background color for export. Applies to: WEBP ('transparent' or any '#RRGGBB'), PNG ('transparent' or any '#RRGGBB').

parameters.name: jpegCompressionMethod
parameters.description: JPEG: Compression method

parameters.name: pngInterlaced
parameters.description: PNG: Interlaced PNG

parameters.name: pdfPresetRole
parameters.description: PDF: Pick a built-in Adobe PDF preset by its locale-independent role. Use this for any built-in preset \u2014 display names are localized (e.g. 'High Quality Print' shows a different name on non-English installs), so a role is the only reliable selector. Wins over pdfPreset if both are set.

parameters.name: pdfPreset
parameters.description: PDF: Pick a custom (user-created) preset by its exact catalog name; for built-in presets use pdfPresetRole. An unknown name fails with the list of installed presets. If neither is set, export reuses the last-used PDF settings (the document's own saved PDF settings, else the app's last export preference).

parameters.name: tiffLzwCompression
parameters.description: TIFF: Enable LZW compression

parameters.name: svgStyling
parameters.description: SVG: How style properties are written. 'inline' puts them in element style attributes (Inline Style), 'css' emits a <style> block with class selectors (Internal CSS), 'presentationAttributes' uses presentation attributes on elements.

parameters.name: svgFont
parameters.description: SVG: How fonts are handled. 'svg' embeds font data as SVG font definitions in the output (SVG), 'outline' converts text to vector outlines eliminating font dependencies (Convert To Outlines).

parameters.name: svgImages
parameters.description: SVG: How raster images are handled. 'embed' encodes images as base64 data URIs, 'link' writes sidecar image files next to the SVG, 'preserve' keeps the original link/embed state from the source document. In outputMode='stream' all modes are normalized to 'embed' so the returned SVG is self-contained.

parameters.name: aiIncludeLinkedFiles
parameters.description: AI: When true, embeds linked images and placed EPS files into the saved AI file. When false, no additional embedding occurs \u2014 files that are currently linked remain linked, but already-embedded content is not affected.

parameters.name: collisionStrategy
parameters.description: How to handle an existing file at outputPath. When no leaf filename is given (path ends in a separator or resolves to an existing directory), 'error' is changed to 'autoSuffix' \u2014 UNLESS you explicitly pass 'overwrite', which is still honored for a derived leaf. 'error' (default) fails the call and surfaces the conflict to the user \u2014 ALWAYS use this when you supplied an explicit leaf filename; do NOT silently rename or replace it. 'overwrite' replaces the existing file \u2014 permitted ONLY when the user's current message explicitly instructs you to overwrite or replace it (e.g. 'overwrite it', 'replace the file'). Re-issuing the same export request, even to the same path, expresses export intent, not overwrite permission; nor does a prior overwrite approval or a path you chose earlier in this task. 'autoSuffix' appends '-2', '-3', ... until unique \u2014 this is also the default fallback for a derived leaf when 'overwrite' was not requested; with an explicit leaf filename, set it yourself ONLY to stay collision-safe when iterating over multiple objects. When in doubt with an explicit filename, use 'error' and ask the user.

tools.name: CapturePreview
tools.description: Captures artwork as a PNG file for visual inspection. Returns a preview_path field with the file location \u2014 read that file to view the image. For permanent file exports (PNG/JPEG/SVG/PDF), use Export instead. Use this to verify your work AFTER completing a batch of related changes. Avoid calling more than 2-3 times per task unless debugging a specific visual issue. width/height control max output dimensions in pixels (max 1024 each, total pixel area capped at 512x512). To inspect a specific region at higher detail, use cropX/cropY/cropWidth/cropHeight to specify a bounding box in points. Default target is CANVAS.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.description: Brief reason for this visual check (e.g., 'verify layout after placing all stat cards')

parameters.name: targetType
parameters.description: One of: CANVAS, SELECTION, ARTBOARD, or UUID. Default: CANVAS (entire document).

parameters.name: uuids
parameters.description: UUIDs of objects, groups, or layers to capture. Pass one or more UUIDs when targetType=UUID. Get UUIDs from GetCanvasStructure. Always pass an array, even for one object.

parameters.name: artboardIndex
parameters.description: 1-based artboard index from ListArtboards (1 = first artboard). Omit to use the active artboard.

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: Max width of the exported image in pixels (default: 400, maximum: 1024). Total pixel area is capped at 512*512.

parameters.name: height
parameters.description: Max height of the exported image in pixels (default: 400, maximum: 1024). Total pixel area is capped at 512*512.

parameters.name: cropX
parameters.description: Crop region left edge in points (canvas-global, Y-down). When cropWidth and cropHeight are both > 0, only this rectangular area is captured. Use GetActiveArtboard to find artboard bounds.

parameters.name: cropY
parameters.description: Crop region top edge in points (canvas-global, Y-down).

parameters.name: cropWidth
parameters.description: Crop region width in points. 0 = no crop (use full target bounds).

parameters.name: cropHeight
parameters.description: Crop region height in points. 0 = no crop (use full target bounds).

tools.name: Extract
tools.description: Extract named resources ('what': colors, swatches, symbols, brushes, graphic-styles, character-styles, or paragraph-styles) from a document at an absolute file path into the current document. 'filters' is an optional comma-separated list narrowing results; allowed values depend on 'what' (brushes: used,unused,calligraphic,scatter,art,bristle,pattern; symbols: used,unused,static,dynamic; graphic-styles/character-styles/paragraph-styles: used,unused; colors/swatches: used,unused,process,global,spot,solid,pattern,linear-gradient,radial-gradient,gradient). A result only carries the fields for axes you actually filtered: omitting an axis skips its field (and, for usage, its scan) -- cheapest, still matches everything; giving any value(s) from an axis (even all of them) adds that axis's field ('type' or 'used') to every result. So to learn everything about a 'what' with full classification in one call, list every value of the axis/axes you need rather than omitting them (e.g. filters=\\\"used,unused,static,dynamic\\\" for symbols) -- free for kind/type, but usage costs a full document scan, so skip both used/unused if you don't need that field. Notes: process+global = solid colors only (excludes gradients/patterns; solid+pattern+gradient = all); prefer 'gradient' over listing linear-gradient+radial-gradient together; never combine 'gradient' with either subtype (it already implies both); 'spot' is a subset of 'global' -- don't combine them. Always pass dryRun:true unless the user explicitly wants the resources copied into the current document -- omitting dryRun (or passing false) performs a real, document-mutating extraction, not a preview. Any list/what/show/describe/summarize-style question about a file's contents requires dryRun:true, even when falling back to Extract after a different tool (e.g. an attachment-inspection or summarization agent) failed to answer that same question -- a failed prior tool does not turn a listing request into an import request. dryRun never modifies anything and honors 'filters' identically. Never call Extract without dryRun more than once per request for the same 'what', and don't fall back to a different/empty filter just to keep exploring; a 0-result response is final. If an unfiltered dryRun for a 'what' already returns 0, that 'what' has none in the file -- don't retry with filters. Returns JSON describing the resources that would be (dryRun) or were (real call) extracted.

parameters.name: filePath
parameters.description: Absolute path to the file to extract from.

parameters.name: what
parameters.description: Resource type to extract.

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description: Comma-separated filters narrowing which resources to extract; allowed values depend on 'what'. Invalid values are ignored with a warning. Omit to extract everything of the given type.

parameters.name: dryRun
parameters.description: If true, reports which resources would be extracted without changing the current document -- nothing is imported.

tools.name: FindObjects
tools.description: Batch query and update tool for object properties (color, weight, font, text content). Prefer over structural browsing when you need bulk data (e.g. every object's color for grouping or auditing) \u2014 omit matchCriteria, pass returnFields:['color'] to get all fill/stroke values in one call without walking the hierarchy. Also finds objects by exact criteria (not fuzzy/visual categories \u2014 'lines' aren't a distinct type from other paths, see 'objectTypes') and optionally writes setProperties (fillColor/strokeColor/strokeWeight) onto every match in the same call. setProperties can never write text content (use ReplaceText) or font (use ReplaceFont). Omit 'setProperties' to run in query mode: matches are reported (shape controlled by 'returnFields') and nothing is written. Provide 'setProperties' to write onto every match instead \u2014 its keys don't need to match matchCriteria's 1:1 (e.g. match fillColor, set strokeWeight). Omit 'matchCriteria' to target every object matching 'objectTypes' unconditionally, in either mode. Write mode: locked/hidden objects are matched but never written to (reported in failed_objects). Query mode: the walk may stop at the response size limit \u2014 success_count reflects matches found so far, not necessarily every match in the document.

parameters.name: objectTypes
parameters.description: Omit to visit every object in the document \u2014 the default when targeting all objects. Provide objectTypes only when the request explicitly names a specific category: 'path' (paths, compound paths), 'mesh' (gradient meshes \u2014 fill-only, no stroke), 'text' (text frames). Always pass an array, even for one type.

parameters.name: matchCriteria
parameters.description: Criteria to match, e.g. {\\\"fillColor\\\":\\\"#FF0000\\\"}, {\\\"strokeWeight\\\":2}, {\\\"fontFamily\\\":\\\"Myriad Pro\\\"}, {\\\"searchText\\\":\\\"Lorem ipsum\\\"}. Keys: fillColor/strokeColor (hex '#RRGGBB', swatch {\\\"model\\\":\\\"swatch\\\",\\\"name\\\":\\\"PANTONE 485 C\\\"}, color {model:'cmyk'|'rgb'|'gray',...}, or 'none'), strokeWeight (number), fontFamily/fontStyle (strings, checked against document usage not installed fonts; require objectTypes 'text' or omitted), searchText (string, same search as ReplaceText \u2014 multiple occurrences in one frame still count as one match; require objectTypes 'text' or omitted), caseSensitive/wholeWord (booleans, default true, require searchText). Omit (or pass {}) to match every object visited by 'objectTypes' unconditionally.

parameters.name: setProperties
parameters.description: Values to set on every match. Omit to run in query mode instead. Supports only fillColor/strokeColor/strokeWeight (same formats as 'matchCriteria'). Keys don't need to match matchCriteria's 1:1. At least one key required when provided.

parameters.name: returnFields
parameters.description: Query mode only; rejected with 'setProperties'. Fields per matched object: 'uuid', 'bounds' (GetBounds convention), 'color' ({fill,stroke} \u2014 each a color object or null if unpainted; mesh stroke is always null; mixed objects add fillIsMixed/strokeIsMixed:true when values disagree), 'textRanges' (character offsets of matched runs/occurrences within text frames \u2014 requires matchCriteria fontFamily or searchText; shape: [{start,end},...]; request when a follow-up tool needs sub-frame positions, omit for frame-level queries). Omit 'returnFields' for uuid only \u2014 each extra field costs an additional lookup per match.

parameters.name: startAfterUuid
parameters.description: Resume cursor for a truncated query-mode match list: pass the previous response's resume_after_uuid to continue after that point (only reliable if the document/params are unchanged). Rejected with an error if the uuid isn't found among current matches (e.g. the document changed) \u2014 omit startAfterUuid and retry to start over from the first match instead of guessing. Query mode only.

tools.name: SetGradient
tools.description: Create or patch a gradient on the fill or stroke of one or more objects.\\n\\nCREATE / REPLACE mode \u2014 provide both colors and positions: builds a new gradient with the given stops, replacing any existing one.\\nPATCH mode \u2014 omit both colors and positions: preserves all existing stops (including midpoints), gradient-level properties (interpolation, dither), and geometry (origin, length, matrix). Only the properties you explicitly supply (angle, gradientType) are changed. The object must already have a gradient on the target; returns an error otherwise.\\n\\nProvide both colors+positions together or neither \u2014 mixing is an error.\\nEach stop color may be a hex string ('#RRGGBB' / '#RRGGBBAA' / '#RGB') or a color object (rgb / cmyk / gray / swatch). Positions are 0-100. Never invent, guess, or autocomplete swatch names.\\nText frames: not supported \u2014 returns an error. Convert to outlines first (ExpandArt/CreateOutlines) or have the user drag the Gradient tool interactively.

parameters.name: uuids
parameters.description: UUIDs of the objects to apply gradient to. Always pass an array, even for one object.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.description: Color stops for the gradient (CREATE/REPLACE mode). Minimum 2 stops. Each stop accepts hex sugar ('#FF0000') or an object ({\\\"model\\\":\\\"cmyk\\\",\\\"c\\\":0,\\\"m\\\":1,\\\"y\\\":1,\\\"k\\\":0}). Omit to use PATCH mode (preserve existing stops). Accepts: hex like '#RRGGBB' or '#RGB' (sugar), or an object: {\\\"model\\\":\\\"rgb\\\",\\\"r\\\":1,\\\"g\\\":0,\\\"b\\\":0} | {\\\"model\\\":\\\"cmyk\\\",\\\"c\\\":0,\\\"m\\\":1,\\\"y\\\":1,\\\"k\\\":0} | {\\\"model\\\":\\\"gray\\\",\\\"gray\\\":0.5} | {\\\"model\\\":\\\"swatch\\\",\\\"name\\\":\\\"PANTONE 185 C\\\",\\\"tint\\\":0.5}. The 'none' sentinel is not accepted here. Per-stop opacity is available via the '#RRGGBBAA' string form or an 'opacity' field (0-1) on the object form. Accepts: hex like '#RRGGBB' or '#RGB' (sugar), or an object: {\"model\":\"rgb\",\"r\":1,\"g\":0,\"b\":0} | {\"model\":\"cmyk\",\"c\":0,\"m\":1,\"y\":1,\"k\":0} | {\"model\":\"gray\",\"gray\":0.5} | {\"model\":\"swatch\",\"name\":\"PANTONE 185 C\",\"tint\":0.5}. The 'none' sentinel is not accepted here. Per-stop opacity is available via the '#RRGGBBAA' string form or an 'opacity' field (0\u20131) on the object form.

parameters.name: positions
parameters.description: Ramp positions for each color stop (0-100). Must match colors array length. E.g. [0, 100] for start-to-end. Omit together with colors to use PATCH mode.

parameters.name: gradientType
parameters.description: Gradient type: 'linear' or 'radial'. Omit to preserve existing type (PATCH mode) or default to 'linear' (CREATE mode).

parameters.name: angle
parameters.description: Gradient angle in degrees. 0 = left-to-right, 90 = bottom-to-top, 180 = right-to-left, 270 = top-to-bottom. Only applies to linear gradients. Omit to preserve existing angle (PATCH mode) or default to 0 (CREATE mode).

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: Gradient target: 'fill' (default) or 'stroke'

tools.name: Vectorize
tools.description: Traces a raster or placed image into vectors with Image Trace, or expands an existing live Image Trace into a final vector group. To preserve the user's original, always DUPLICATE the source image first (e.g. with DuplicateObjects) and run this tool on the duplicate's `uuid` \u2014 never trace the original directly. Offset the duplicate so it sits BESIDE the original with a small gap \u2014 not overlapping it (e.g. DuplicateObjects offsetX/offsetY), keeping it within the canvas bounds where possible. (This applies only when `uuid` is a source raster/placed image; when it is already a live tracing you are re-tracing or expanding, operate on it directly \u2014 do not duplicate.) Before tracing, determine what the image actually is \u2014 its content is NOT in the object metadata, so do not guess from it. Unless you have already seen the image this turn, inspect the actual pixels first \u2014 the selected image, or the whole canvas when nothing is selected \u2014 using whatever image-inspection capability you have, then pass the `preset` that matches what you saw. If no preset matches the requested look or exact settings, pick the CLOSEST one, run it as `trace_live` (re-runnable, so the user can review), and say clearly in your reply which preset you used and that it's the closest approximation, not exact. `action` controls the result: by default it stays a LIVE, editable Image Trace (`trace_live`); it is expanded into a final vector group only when the user asks. On success, `trace_and_expand` always consumes the input `uuid` \u2014 use the returned `uuid`. `expand` consumes the input only if it's an existing live Image Trace; otherwise it's a no-op and the input `uuid` remains valid \u2014 see `details`. `trace_live` never consumes the input \u2014 the source is retained (embedded in the tracing), and the returned `uuid` is the (possibly new) tracing object. If a call fails, re-fetch current document state rather than retrying the input `uuid`.

parameters.name: uuid
parameters.description: UUID of the object to operate on (from the canvas/object summary): a raster or placed image to trace, or an existing live Image Trace to expand or re-trace with a different preset. When tracing, this should be a duplicate you created (see the tool description), not the user's original.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: What to do with the object at `uuid`:\\n- trace_live (default): trace into a live, editable Image Trace and LEAVE IT LIVE \u2014 nothing finalized. The trace stays live so the user can review and tune it. If `uuid` is already a live tracing, re-applies the preset.\\n- trace_and_expand: trace, then immediately expand into a final, editable vector group. Use ONLY when the user explicitly asks to finalize / expand / flatten the trace. If `uuid` is already a live tracing, re-applies the preset then expands. This REPLACES the traced object in place \u2014 the resulting group becomes the artwork and that object no longer exists; because you trace a duplicate (see above), the user's original image is preserved.\\n- expand: expand an existing live Image Trace into a final vector group; pass preset 'none'. Use when the user asks to finalize an existing live tracing. If `uuid` isn't a live tracing (e.g. already expanded), report that there's nothing to expand \u2014 don't expand a different object.\\nTo retry with a different preset, do NOT delete the result \u2014 deleting it does not restore the original image; use Undo instead. trace_live (the default) is re-runnable when the preset is uncertain.

parameters.name: preset
parameters.description: The Image Trace preset to apply. For the expand action pass 'none'. For trace_live or trace_and_expand, pick the single preset that best matches the image you inspected \u2014 what it is (photo, logo, icon, line drawing, sketch), how many colors it has, and color vs. grayscale \u2014 not guessed from metadata:\\n- none: no preset; expand action only.\\n- autoColor: full-color trace where Illustrator decides the number of colors. Use only for genuinely full-color or complex images whose colors matter and no more specific preset fits; do not fall back to it when the image content is unclear \u2014 determine the content first.\\n- highColor: full color, high number of colors. For detailed, vivid color art.\\n- lowColor: full color reduced to ~16 colors. For simpler color art or a flatter look.\\n- threeColors: exactly 3 colors. For bold, minimal color graphics.\\n- sixColors: exactly 6 colors. For flat graphics with a small palette.\\n- sixteenColors: exactly 16 colors. For flat graphics, moderate palette.\\n- highFidelityPhoto: full-color photo trace preserving the most detail. For realistic photographs.\\n- lowFidelityPhoto: full-color photo trace with fewer colors. Simpler, posterized photo look.\\n- grayscale: shades of gray. For black-and-white photographs or gray images.\\n- shadesOfGray: grayscale with fewer tones, for a flatter monochrome result.\\n- blackAndWhite: two-tone black and white. For high-contrast images, stamps, or simple marks.\\n- outline: edges as black strokes on transparent bg. For line drawings you want as strokes, not fills.\\n- lineArt: clean black-and-white line work. For crisp inked drawings or comic art.\\n- sketchedArt: black-and-white trace tuned for hand-drawn sketches and pencil work.\\n- technicalDrawing: black-and-white trace for precise, fine-detail line drawings, e.g. blueprints/schematics.\\n- silhouettes: solid black shapes. Bold filled silhouettes.\\n- blackAndWhiteLogo: black-and-white trace tuned for simple logos and marks.

tools.name: CreateLayer
tools.description: Creates a new layer with the specified name. Position defaults to front (top) of the layer stack. Use parentID to create a sublayer inside an existing layer. For 'above:<uuid>' or 'below:<uuid>', the new layer is created as a sibling of the reference layer (same nesting level). Layers cannot be placed inside groups \u2014 only into other layers. Returns the new layer identifier in the top-level `uuid` field.

parameters.name: layerName
parameters.description: Name for the new layer

parameters.name: parentID
parameters.description: UUID of a parent layer to create the sublayer inside. When provided, 'front'/'back' place at top/bottom inside that layer. Ignored when position is 'above:<uuid>' or 'below:<uuid>'. Omit to create at the top level.

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: Where to place in the z-order: 'front' (topmost, default), 'back' (bottommost), 'above:<uuid>' (above referenced object), 'below:<uuid>' (below referenced object). When parentID is provided, 'front'/'back' place inside that container. 'above:<uuid>'/'below:<uuid>' always place relative to the referenced object \u2014 parentID is ignored. tools.name: GetVisualAppearance
tools.description: Get detailed visual appearance properties for one or more objects. Response format: {success, details, visual_appearance: [{uuid, properties: {fill_stack, stroke_stack, has_fill, has_stroke, opacity, blend_mode, graphic_style, mask_context, is_clip_path, hidden, locked}}, ...]}. Each result includes: fill_stack (array), stroke_stack (array), has_fill (boolean), has_stroke (boolean), opacity (number), blend_mode (string), graphic_style (string|null), mask_context (object with is_clipping_mask and clipped_by), is_clip_path (boolean \u2014 true when this path is the clipping mask path inside a clipping group), hidden (boolean), locked (boolean). For gradient fills/strokes, the color entry includes: model='gradient', gradientType, angle, length, origin, and a stops array where each stop has rampPoint (0-100), midPoint, opacity, and a color object. To change only angle or gradientType on an existing gradient, use SetGradient PATCH mode (omit colors+positions entirely \u2014 no need to read stops first). To replace stops while keeping the same count/positions as a reference, read the stops here then rebuild colors[] from each stop's color field and positions[] from each stop's rampPoint, and pass them to SetGradient CREATE mode. Use this when you need to analyze visual styling. To confirm a color/appearance-named target, call this with the candidate UUIDs. BATCH PROCESSING: When analyzing multiple objects, pass array of UUIDs to get all results in one call. LARGE RESPONSES: When results exceed the size limit, partial results are returned with truncated=true and resume_hint with instructions on how to continue.

parameters.name: uuids
parameters.description: UUIDs of objects to query. Always pass an array, even for one object.

tools.name: GetGeometry
tools.description: Get detailed geometry properties for one or more path/shape objects. Response format: {success, details, geometry_refinement: [{uuid, properties: {transformation_matrix?, is_proportionally_scaled?, path_topology}}, ...]}. Fields vary by art type: transformation_matrix (6-element [a,b,c,d,tx,ty] array) and is_proportionally_scaled (bool \u2014 true when scaleX and scaleY differ by less than 2%) are present only for symbol, raster, placed, and text frame art. path_topology for simple paths: {is_closed (bool), segment_count (int)}. path_topology for compound paths: {winding_order (even_odd|non_zero), child_count, path_count, total_segment_count, nested_compound_count}. Use this when you need to analyze geometric construction. BATCH PROCESSING: When analyzing multiple paths, pass array of UUIDs to get all results in one call. LARGE RESPONSES: When results exceed the size limit, partial results are returned with truncated=true and resume_hint with instructions on how to continue.

parameters.name: uuids

Response format: {success, details, typography_metrics: [{uuid, properties: {...}}, ...]}. Each result properties: text_length (number), text_content? (string), has_text_overflow? (boolean), font_runs (array of font entries \u2014 each entry: {font_family (string), font_style? (string), is_font_missing (boolean \u2014 true when the font is substituted or unavailable), is_font_embeddable (boolean \u2014 true when font permits embedding)}; always present for text frames; empty array for empty frames, 1 entry for single-font frames, multiple entries for mixed-font frames; use this to enumerate ALL fonts in a text frame), font_family? (deprecated, same as font_runs[0].font_family), font_style? (deprecated, same as font_runs[0].font_style), is_font_missing? (deprecated, same as font_runs[0].is_font_missing), is_font_embeddable? (deprecated, same as font_runs[0].is_font_embeddable), font_caps? (string: normal|all_caps|small_caps|all_small_caps \u2014 ATE capitalization option for the story; rendered case may differ from text_content, e.g. all_caps with stored lowercase), font_size? (number), tracking? (number), kerning? (string), leading? (number), leading_type? (string), auto_leading? (boolean), baseline_shift? (number), paragraph_alignment? (string), horizontal_scale? (number, percentage 0-100+), vertical_scale? (number, percentage 0-100+). Callers must not assume any ? property is present. BATCH PROCESSING: When analyzing multiple text frames, pass array of UUIDs to get all results in one call.
