tools.name: GetDynamicEffects
tools.description: Get dynamic effects applied to one or more objects. Response format: {success, details, dynamic_effects: [{uuid, properties: {effects: [{type, title, enabled, category, paint_index?, parameters?}]}}, ...]}. Each effect object contains: type (effect identifier string), title (display name), enabled (boolean), category (pre_effect/post_effect/paint_effect), paint_index (number, for paint effects only), and parameters (known per-effect parameters when available). For supported effects, parameters include values such as drop shadow offsets/color/opacity/darkness and gaussian blur radius. Empty effects array means no effects applied. BATCH PROCESSING: When checking effects on multiple objects, pass array of UUIDs to get all results in one call. LARGE RESPONSES: When results exceed the size limit, partial results are returned with truncated=true and resume_hint with instructions on how to continue.

parameters.name: uuids
parameters.description: UUIDs of objects to query. Always pass an array, even for one object.

tools.name: GetObjectStructure
tools.description: Get recursive structure for one or more objects (including layers). Returns 'structures' array. Each entry: uuid, name, object_type, bounds, locked (when true), hidden (when true) \u2014 both inherited from ancestors; is_generative (when true), generative_type (when present), has_edit_lineage (when true). Bounds are visual bounds that include live effect expansion (e.g. Gaussian blur expands bounds beyond the path geometry). Bounds may be absent for empty groups. Text objects also include text_content (the full text string). Groups and layers have children (array, z-order: 0=topmost) and child_count. Use maxDepth to limit recursion (groups/layers at max depth show child_count + child_types summary instead of children). Use includeTypes to filter \u2014 only matching types appear; groups/layers are always traversed to find matches within the traversed depth. NOTE: includeTypes only matches objects reached within maxDepth \u2014 if matching objects exist inside nested groups beyond maxDepth they will not appear. Use maxDepth=-1 to find all matching objects regardless of nesting. Example: maxDepth=2, includeTypes=['text'] finds text objects up to 2 levels deep. CRITICAL: Use this to drill into groups and layers from GetCanvasStructure/GetArtboardStructure. BATCH: Pass array of UUIDs. LARGE RESPONSES: When the response size limit is reached, expansion stops \u2014 groups already listed retain child_count/child_types for navigation. Results include truncated=true and resume_hint. Call GetObjectStructure on specific group UUIDs to drill deeper. RESUME: truncation can happen at ANY depth, not just the top level a UUID was requested with \u2014 recursively scan every node in 'structures' (including nested 'children', however deep) for partial:true and resume EACH one individually via uuids=[that node's uuid], startAfterUuid=<its resume_after_uuid> (see the startAfterUuid parameter for how multiple uuids/cursors combine in one call). If a node has partial:true but NO resume_after_uuid, either that group's expansion stopped before any child was returned, or (for a text object) its text_content was dropped to fit the size limit (text_length still reflects the true length) \u2014 either way, retry with uuids=[that uuid] and no startAfterUuid to get it fresh with its own budget. A uuid in remaining_uuids that is NOT itself marked partial anywhere was never touched at all \u2014 re-call with uuids=[that uuid] alone, no cursor needed. RESUME PATTERN \u2014 to FULLY expand a list of uuids you MUST drain BOTH mechanisms until nothing is truncated or partial. A single response can carry remaining_uuids AND nested partial:true nodes at the same time; handling only one leaves objects uncollected. Keep two queues: 'cursored' (partial nodes to resume, each with its own resume_after_uuid) and 'fresh' (uuids not yet reached, seeded with the uuids you want to expand). Loop until both are empty. Example Python:\\ndef find_partials(nodes):\\n    found, stack = [], list(nodes or [])\\n    while stack:\\n        n = stack.pop()\\n        if n.get(\\\"partial\\\"):\\n            found.append((n[\\\"uuid\\\"], n.get(\\\"resume_after_uuid\\\")))\\n        stack.extend(n.get(\\\"children\\\") or [])\\n    return found\\ncursored, fresh, structures = [], list(target_uuids), []\\nwhile cursored or fresh:\\n    kwargs = {\\\"includeTypes\\\": [\\\"text\\\"], \\\"maxDepth\\\": \\\"-1\\\"}\\n    if cursored:\\n        uuid, cursor = cursored.pop(0)\\n        kwargs[\\\"uuids\\\"] = [uuid] + fresh\\n        fresh = []\\n        if cursor:\\n            kwargs[\\\"startAfterUuid\\\"] = cursor\\n    else:\\n        kwargs[\\\"uuids\\\"], fresh = fresh, []\\n    res = GetObjectStructure(**kwargs)\\n    structures.extend(res.get(\\\"structures\\\") or [])\\n    cursored += find_partials(res.get(\\\"structures\\\") or [])\\n    fresh += res.get(\\\"remaining_uuids\\\") or []\\nThen filter 'structures' (recursively over children) by object_type for your target objects.

parameters.name: uuids
parameters.description: UUIDs of objects to query. Always pass an array, even for one object.

parameters.name: maxDepth
parameters.description: Maximum recursion depth for groups. -1 = unlimited (default). 0 = root object only, no children expanded. 1 = immediate children only. 2+ = deeper. Groups at maxDepth show child_count and child_types summary.

parameters.name: includeTypes
parameters.description: Filter: only include objects of these types in children. Groups and layers are always traversed to find matching descendants. Empty = no filter.

parameters.name: startAfterUuid
parameters.description: Resume cursor for re-expanding a group whose children were previously cut short. This ONE cursor value is checked against EACH requested top-level uuid's OWN direct children, in the order given: whichever uuid's children actually contain it resumes from the NEXT sibling after it, and that consumes the cursor \u2014 every OTHER uuid in the same call (whether listed before or after the match) is simply expanded fresh from its own first child instead, which is the expected behavior, not an error. This means you can safely combine one resuming (partial) uuid together with any number of fresh/untouched uuids in a single call. If no uuid in the call contains a match at all, every uuid is expanded fresh from its own first child. Only affects the direct children of the top-level uuids in THIS call, not nested descendants. Empty = start every uuid fresh from the first child as usual.

tools.name: GetBounds
tools.description: Get bounds for one or more objects. Returns visual bounds that include live effect expansion (e.g. a Gaussian blur with radius=20 expands bounds ~36pt per side). Empty groups/layers have no bounds and are reported in failed_objects. Lightweight alternative to GetGeometry for layout calculations. Supports batch via uuids array. Coordinates are canvas-global in points with Y-down. LARGE RESPONSES: When results exceed the size limit, partial results are returned with truncated=true and resume_hint with instructions on how to continue.

parameters.name: uuids
parameters.description: UUIDs of objects to query. Always pass an array, even for one object.

tools.name: PathfinderOperation
tools.description: Performs boolean operations (unite, minus_front, minus_back, intersect, exclude) on two or more objects \u2014 paths, compound paths, text frames, and groups can all be mixed in the same call. Cannot mix hidden and visible objects in the same call \u2014 a hidden object (or one inside a hidden layer) is excluded rather than included. Locked objects (or ones inside a locked layer) are excluded too \u2014 ask the user to unlock first if it must be included. The first object in the array (index 0) is the base shape: for unite/intersect/exclude its fill/stroke appearance is what the result inherits; for minus_front/minus_back it is the object that survives, with the remaining objects (index 1+) subtracted from it. UUIDs consumed by a successful operation are unusable afterward \u2014 use the returned `uuid`. If the call fails, re-fetch current document state rather than retrying the input UUIDs. An object that doesn't exist is reported via fail_count/failed_objects; a locked or hidden object via skipped_count/skipped_objects (both {uuid, reason}) and remains valid. Either way the whole call doesn't fail, unless the excluded object was the base shape (index 0) for minus_front/minus_back, or fewer than 2 valid objects remain.

parameters.name: uuids
parameters.description: UUIDs of path objects. Minimum 2 required. First object is the base shape. Always pass an array, even for one object.

parameters.name: operation
parameters.description: Boolean operation to perform.

tools.name: CleanupPath
tools.description: Cleans up messy or hand-drawn paths by reducing anchor points and/or smoothing jaggedness. This EDITS geometry \u2014 it approximates the original shape within a tolerance, it does not preserve it exactly. Higher curvePrecision / lower smoothingPercentage = closer to the original but less cleanup; lower curvePrecision / higher smoothingPercentage = more aggressive cleanup but more shape drift. mode='simplify': reduces the number of anchor points within a curve-fit tolerance (same as Object > Path > Simplify) \u2014 use when a path has too many/dense anchor points. In mode='simplify' (only), pointsAfter is guaranteed never to exceed pointsBefore: at a very high curvePrecision the curve-fit can technically need more anchors than it started with, in which case that path is left as it was rather than made worse. If pointsAfter equals pointsBefore, pass a lower curvePrecision and re-call to actually reduce anchors \u2014 omitting curvePrecision uses the application's Simplify preference (often high/conservative) and will not by itself reduce anchors further. mode='smooth': repositions anchor points/handles to remove jaggedness WITHOUT reducing point count (same as the Smooth tool) \u2014 use when lines look jagged, rough, or hand-drawn. mode='both' (default): smooths first, then simplifies the result \u2014 use for general 'clean up this path' / 'make the lines cleaner' requests. The pointsAfter<=pointsBefore guarantee above only covers the simplify step itself; if smoothing increases anchor count, the final pointsAfter can still exceed the original pointsBefore. curvePrecision/angleThreshold/smoothingPercentage are optional. When curvePrecision is omitted, the application's Simplify preference (GetTolerance) is used. When angleThreshold is omitted, the application's Simplify preference (GetAngleThresold) is used. When smoothingPercentage is omitted, it auto-calibrates per path (same as the Smooth tool's default). Only affects anchors that are curve points; anchors explicitly marked as corner points (e.g. straight polygon-style paths with no curve handles) are intentionally left untouched by design \u2014 this matches Illustrator's own Simplify/Smooth, which never round off a rectangle's corners either. If a call reports success but pointsBefore equals pointsAfter with no meaningful bounds change, the path is likely all corner points and not a candidate for cleanup. Only path objects with 3+ anchor points are eligible \u2014 groups, compound paths, text, and paths with fewer anchors are skipped, not treated as failures (reported in `results` with skipped=true and a reason). For groups, use GetObjectStructure to expand to path children first, then pass those uuids \u2014 compound paths and text cannot be decomposed into individual paths by any tool and are simply not supported. Returns per-object anchor-point counts and bounding boxes before/after \u2014 YOU are responsible for checking that delta and re-calling with lower precision/percentage (or telling the user) if the shape drifted more than intended; the tool does not enforce shape fidelity itself.

parameters.name: uuids
parameters.description: UUIDs of path objects to clean up. Always pass an array, even for one object.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Cleanup mode: 'simplify' reduces anchor point count, 'smooth' removes jaggedness without changing point count, 'both' smooths then simplifies.

parameters.name: curvePrecision
parameters.description: Simplify curve-fit precision (0-100, higher = closer fit = more points kept). Used when mode is 'simplify' or 'both'. For genuinely jagged/wobbly hand-drawn input, values above ~20 often produce NO visible reduction \u2014 check pointsAfter in the response, and if it didn't drop, retry with a lower value (single digits if needed) rather than assuming it worked. A path with truly chaotic, independent-random anchor placement (not the smoother back-and-forth wobble of a real hand tremor) may still resist a large reduction even at low curvePrecision \u2014 that's an inherent curve-fitting limit (more erratic input needs more control points to represent within any tolerance), not a parameter to keep lowering indefinitely. Omit curvePrecision to use the application's Simplify preference instead of guessing.

parameters.name: angleThreshold
parameters.description: Simplify corner-preservation angle threshold in degrees (0-180). Used when mode is 'simplify' or 'both'. Omit to use the application default.

parameters.name: smoothingPercentage
parameters.description: Smoothing strength (0-100, same scale as the Smooth tool/pathItem.smootheningPercentage). Used when mode is 'smooth' or 'both'. Omit to auto-calibrate per path.

tools.name: RunPreflightChecks
tools.description: Single-traversal production QA inspection of the active document. Walks the art tree once and returns a categorized JSON report of findings aggregated by issue tag, each with a display_name, count, and affected_objects[] array; UUIDs and raw fact fields (effective PPI, stroke widths, font license types, etc.) are per affected object, not per aggregated finding. Available scopes: document (color mode, profile, bleed, units, metadata, artboard checks), images (resolution, embedded size, pixel dimensions, color space, missing embedded ICC on linked placed rasters), links (broken, modified, damaged), text (fonts: missing, embeddability, license; text frames: overset, sizing, scaling, leading), colors (fill/stroke colors, spot colors, strokes, overprint white/black/non-black, rich black CMYK detection, raster effects), objects (scale, visibility, position, empty groups, locked state, objects near trim edge / bleed extension). Only the requested scopes are executed and emitted in the response \u2014 use this to focus on a specific concern and reduce response size. Omit `scopes` (or pass an empty array) to run all domains. Response shape: top-level `checks` object keyed by category (document/images/links/text/colors/objects), each with a `findings` array (+ optional `partial: true`); top-level `summary` object holds counts and context (total_issues, categories_with_issues, document_context, scopes). `details` is a short human-readable status line (e.g. \\\"findings=3 categories=2\\\") meant for logging/display. Read findings from `checks.<category>.findings` and counts from `summary`. Tool returns raw facts only \u2014 findings are pre-aggregated by issue tag with `display_name` and `affected_objects[]`. No severity in JSON. PREFLIGHT SEVERITY: Classify per the user's stated output moment (print/export/share/screen). If the user did not state a moment, derive it from the document context in the response: is_print_doc=true \u2192 treat as print; is_print_doc=false \u2192 treat as screen. If is_print_doc is absent or ambiguous, default to print. Always state which moment you assumed and why. Must fix: the violation is irreversible at output time regardless of designer intent. Needs review: threshold violated but correctness depends on designer intent or context. Always classify as Needs review regardless of output moment: text_size_minimum, stroke_hairline, dash_too_short, overprint_on_non_black, zero_dimension_object, object_too_close_to_trim_edge. What's fine: positive observations (e.g. fonts present, color mode correct) \u2014 derive from what the tool did NOT report; never place failed findings here; omit this section entirely when you have no positive observations to make. Scope selection from the user's prompt: targeted request that names ONE attribute \u2192 pass matching `scopes` and report ONLY that attribute (do NOT expand into adjacent prepress checks even if returned; surface any extras as a single footnote line). Multi-attribute request (2+ named attributes, e.g. 'check color mode, bleed, spot colors, and hairline strokes') \u2192 pass all matching scopes for ALL named attributes; Broad request ('full preflight', 'list issues by severity', 'is this file good to go', or no specific attribute) \u2192 omit `scopes` and report EVERY finding the tool returned. Tool returns raw facts only \u2014 findings are pre-aggregated by issue tag with `display_name` and `affected_objects[]`. No severity in JSON. Agent classifies each finding per the SCOPE DISCIPLINE \u2014 PREFLIGHT SEVERITY policy in the system prompt. Each affected_objects[] entry contains uuid (when object-scoped), name, and issue-specific raw fields (e.g., effective_ppi, stroke_width, font_family). checks_skipped: optional array of checks that could not run due to suite errors or unavailability. Each entry has 'check' (tag) and 'reason'. IMPORTANT: an empty findings category is only trustworthy when checks_skipped contains no entry for that category. Final response (agent narrative): open with one sentence using `total_issues` from the summary (count of distinct issue types) and the output moment (e.g. '8 issues need attention before printing.'). Then emit up to 3 labelled sections in this order: **Critical Issues: N**, **Warnings: N**, and **Passed Checks** (no count \u2014 derived from absences of failed findings in scopes that were actually run; reference `checks_skipped` to avoid claiming a check passed when it was skipped). Skip **Critical Issues** or **Warnings** when N = 0. If Critical Issues and Warnings are both zero say 'Your file is production ready. No issues found.' and still include the Passed Checks section listing what was verified. Each finding (and each Passed Checks entry) is a single numbered line: N. {display_name} \u2014 {one-line action or consequence, or for Passed Checks: one-line confirmation of what passed}. No sub-lists. No bold heading per finding. No emojis. Restart numbering at 1 in Warnings and Passed Checks. Do NOT replace the numbered-list-of-findings with a single markdown table whose rows are the findings themselves; a per-finding affected-objects table as supplementary detail beneath a numbered finding line is OK, but the numbered line is required. Severity classification is principle-based (output moment + missing/render-breaking vs context-dependent) per the system prompt's PREFLIGHT SEVERITY policy \u2014 do not consult a static issue-to-tier table. Does not cover vision-only checks (contrast, visual alignment) or checks needing export-format context (transparency flattening). Use this for ANY readiness/verification request \u2014 prompts phrased with check / inspect / audit / verify / validate against document attributes (color mode, profile, bleed, resolution, units, artboard sizes, hidden or locked layers within export-range artboards, fonts, linked images, embedded images, text sizing/overset, spot colors, hairline strokes, overprint, transparency), as well as bare 'check this' / 'run a preflight' / 'production QA' / 'is it ready for print|export|share' / 'verify ... for print output'.

Example: [\\\"images\\\", \\\"links\\\"] runs only image-resolution and broken-link checks. Unknown values are silently ignored.

tools.description: Style-preserving find and replace within a text frame. Replaced text inherits the original character styles. Occurrences using missing/substituted fonts, embedded glyph-subset fonts, or spanning mixed character styles are skipped by default (see skipped_occurrences and action_required). When the target font lacks glyphs for the replacement script, a system fallback font is applied automatically and reported in fallback_fonts_applied (array). If no fallback covers the script, render_warning is set and unfixable_occurrences lists which occurrence(s) are affected. Omit searchText to replace the entire frame content.

parameters.name: uuid
parameters.description: UUID of the text frame

parameters.name: searchText
parameters.description: Text to find (case-sensitive by default). If wholeWord is false, typographic variants (curly quotes, em-dashes) are normalized to ASCII and retried as a fallback, but only when the exact text finds zero matches. Omit to replace the entire text frame content.

parameters.name: replaceText
parameters.description: Replacement text

parameters.name: caseSensitive
parameters.description: When true (default), matching is case-sensitive. When false, matching ignores case (e.g. 'cafe' matches 'CAFE'). Accents are always significant.

parameters.name: occurrences
parameters.description: 0-based indices of occurrences to replace (e.g. [0,2] replaces the 1st and 3rd match). Omit to replace all occurrences. An empty array is an error.

parameters.name: forceReplace
parameters.description: When true, replace ALL occurrences even if they use missing (substituted) fonts, embedded glyph-subset fonts (subset is replaced with the system default), or span mixed character styles. parameters.name: fontFamily
parameters.description: Font family or PostScript name (e.g. 'Myriad Pro', 'MyriadPro-Regular'). Leave empty to keep current font.

parameters.name: fontSize
parameters.description: Font size (0.1-1296). Unit depends on fontSizeUnit (default: points). Omit to keep current size.

parameters.name: verticalScale
parameters.description: Vertical scale percentage (e.g. 100 = 100%, 150 = 150%). Omit to keep current.

parameters.name: kerning
parameters.description: Kerning mode: 'auto', 'optical', 'metricsRomanOnly', or 'none' (disables auto kerning). Omit for no change.

parameters.name: leading
parameters.description: Line spacing in points. 0 = auto leading. Omit for no change.

parameters.description: Space before each paragraph in points. Omit for no change.

parameters.name: spaceAfter
parameters.description: Space after each paragraph in points. Omit for no change.

parameters.name: firstLineIndent

After conversion, the text is no longer editable as text \u2014 it becomes paths/compound paths. Use this before PathfinderOperation on text, or when you need text as vector shapes for effects or clipping. Input UUIDs are unusable once converted \u2014 use that object's outline `uuid` (matched via `original_uuid`). If the call fails, re-fetch current document state rather than retrying the input UUIDs. Returns `outlines`: array of {`uuid`, `original_uuid`, `bounds`} per converted text object.

parameters.name: uuids
parameters.description: UUIDs of text objects to convert to outlines. Always pass an array, even for one object.

tools.name: GetFonts
tools.description: Inspect fonts, including which fonts are MISSING (used in the document but not installed on this system). This is the correct tool to answer 'what fonts are missing?', 'are any fonts missing?', or 'which fonts does this document use?': set documentFonts=true to list every font used in the current document with an 'available' flag (available=false means that font is MISSING). Do not try to read missing fonts from the canvas structure or a screenshot \u2014 they do not report font availability. Also verifies availability of specific fonts by name, or searches installed font families by substring. Does NOT check font embeddability or licensing \u2014 for questions about non-embeddable, license-restricted, or output-readiness fonts, use RunPreflightChecks with scopes=['text'] instead.

parameters.name: fontName
parameters.description: Font family or PostScript names to check (e.g. ['Futura', 'Noto Sans', 'MyriadPro-Regular']). Returns available true/false and PostScript names for each. Use this when you have specific font names to check. Mutually exclusive with 'filter'/'documentFonts' \u2014 pass only one of the three per call.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring search against installed font family names (typeface list) \u2014 searches the list once and returns matching families with their PostScript names. Example: 'arial' matches 'Arial', 'Arial Black', 'Arial Unicode MS'. Mutually exclusive with 'fontName'/'documentFonts' \u2014 pass only one of the three per call.

parameters.name: documentFonts
parameters.description: List every font actually used in the current document by PostScript name, each with 'available' (false means not installed on this system, i.e. a MISSING font). Set this true to report which fonts are missing. Mutually exclusive with 'fontName'/'filter'.

tools.name: ReplaceFont
tools.description: Find every occurrence of one font in the active document and replace it with another, leaving other fonts in mixed-font text frames untouched. Operates document-wide. 'findFontFamily'/'findFontStyle' match only what's actually used in the document, never whether it's installed (so a substituted/missing font can still be found and replaced) \u2014 empty findFontStyle matches any style of the family. 'replaceFontFamily'/'replaceFontStyle' must be installed. Response reports success_count (text frames with at least one matching run), fail_count, and failed_objects ({uuid, reason}).

parameters.name: findFontFamily
parameters.description: Font family or PostScript name to find (e.g. 'Myriad Pro').

parameters.name: findFontStyle
parameters.description: Style variant of the font to find, e.g. 'Bold'. Leave empty to match any style of the family.

parameters.name: replaceFontFamily
parameters.description: Font family or PostScript name to replace with.

parameters.name: replaceFontStyle
parameters.description: Style variant to apply, e.g. 'Bold'. Leave empty when replaceFontFamily is a PostScript name.

tools.name: MoveObjects
tools.description: Do NOT use this tool to CREATE or ADJUST alignment, distribution, or spacing between objects (see DistributeObjects/AlignObjects, which compute the correct offsets directly) -- fine for repositioning a group as a unit ('absolute' mode explicitly preserves existing spacing between the moved objects). Move or place one or more art objects. x and y are each optional; omit one to leave that axis unchanged. TWO MODES: (1) 'relative' (default): x/y are shift distances added to every object. Example: x=50, y=0 nudges objects 50pt right. (2) 'absolute': x/y set the top-left corner of the combined bounding box to that canvas position, preserving spacing between objects. Prefer 'absolute' when you have a target position. Coordinates are canvas-global in points with Y-down.

parameters.name: uuids
parameters.description: UUIDs of the objects to move. Layer UUIDs are not supported. Always pass an array, even for one object.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: Relative mode: horizontal shift in points (positive=right). Absolute mode: target left coordinate for the combined bounding box. Omit to preserve current horizontal position.

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: Relative mode: vertical shift in points (positive=down). Absolute mode: target top coordinate for the combined bounding box. Omit to preserve current vertical position.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: How x/y are interpreted: 'relative' (default) shifts objects by x/y distances, 'absolute' places the combined bounding box top-left at (x,y).

tools.name: RotateObjects
tools.description: Rotate one or more art objects by a specified angle in degrees around the center of their combined bounding box. Example: angle=90 rotates 90 degrees counterclockwise, angle=-45 rotates 45 degrees clockwise.

parameters.name: uuids
parameters.description: UUIDs of the objects to rotate. Layer UUIDs are not supported. Always pass an array, even for one object.

parameters.name: angle
parameters.description: Angle to rotate in degrees (positive = counterclockwise)

tools.name: ScaleObjects
tools.description: Scale one or more art objects around the center of their combined bounding box, preserving relative positions. MODES: 'factor' (default) sx/sy are multipliers (2=double, 0.5=half, 1=no change); 'absolute' sx/sy are target width/height in points \u2014 prefer 'absolute' when you have a target size. If the user names only ONE axis ('scale the width to 2x'), pass just that axis and OMIT the other - it scales uniformly (naming an axis picks which number is given, it does NOT freeze the other). Set maintainAspectRatio=false (needs both sx and sy) when the user gives explicit values for BOTH axes at an unequal ratio ('4in wide and 6in tall', '2x wide and 1.5x tall'), OR uses distortion words (stretch/squash/distort/ignore aspect ratio), OR pins an axis (only/just/'leave the height'). Otherwise keep the default true. Not for use during cleanup/organization tasks - only when the user explicitly requests a visual change.

parameters.name: uuids
parameters.description: UUIDs of the objects to scale. Layer UUIDs are not supported. Always pass an array, even for one object.

parameters.name: sx
parameters.description: Horizontal factor (factor mode) or target width in points (absolute mode). Omit to derive from sy, preserving proportions.

parameters.name: sy
parameters.description: Vertical factor (factor mode) or target height in points (absolute mode). Omit to derive from sx, preserving proportions.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: 'factor' (default): sx/sy are multipliers. 'absolute': sx/sy are target dimensions in points.

parameters.name: maintainAspectRatio
parameters.description: Default true (see tool description for when to set false). With both sx and sy given, applies one uniform scale to both axes: the smaller magnitude of sx/sy in factor mode (per-axis sign kept, so a mirror stays mirrored), or the smaller sx/sy-to-current-size ratio in absolute mode (fits within the target). False applies sx and sy exactly/independently (may distort) and requires both sx and sy - if only one axis is given, this must stay true (the default); setting it false with a single axis is rejected as invalid.

tools.name: RecolorArtwork
tools.description: Remaps the color palette of vector artwork objects as a group using a Firefly-generated palette driven by a theme or mood prompt \u2014 use for palette, mood, tone, aesthetic, or style changes (e.g. 'make it warmer', 'recolor to autumn', 'more vibrant', 'ocean-like', 'cyberpunk neon'). Extracts prominent colors across all objects and remaps them together, preserving visual relationships. Use only for open-ended mood/theme changes: it generates a palette and cannot hit an exact value. If the request names the literal color(s) to end up with \u2014 a hex, a Pantone/spot name, 'all red', or a color space like 'grayscale'/'black and white' \u2014 use SetAppearance instead. The response's resultingColors field lists the distinct new colors the engine produced and applied (across all recolored objects, symbol instances and mesh nodes included). It is the authoritative record of the applied colors: read it to judge whether the palette matches the request, not what you expected. Do NOT capture a preview to check or second-guess the colors \u2014 a preview cannot report them more accurately than resultingColors and, being low-resolution, will often report them wrong (e.g. a deep navy read as a lighter blue), which only misleads you into a needless read-back or re-color. If resultingColorsOmitted is present, that many more colors were applied but dropped for compactness \u2014 judge the palette from the list, but don't call it the complete set. Requires network and consumes Firefly credits, so calls are expensive \u2014 minimize them. Output is generative and varies between calls. Before the first call, if the request gives no usable direction at all \u2014 no mood, hue, reference, or example to build a stylePrompt from (e.g. 'make it look nicer', 'change the colors') \u2014 ask the user what look or mood they want instead of guessing; a vague request won't be fixed by retrying, only by asking. HARD LIMIT: at most two calls per distinct recolor target, counting both successes and failures. This budget is per target, not per message: a message asking for several independent recolors (e.g. 'give the sky an autumn palette and make the mountains more vibrant') gets two calls for each. After a successful call for a target, stop calling for that target. Make a second call ONLY if resultingColors conflict with the request \u2014 wrong hue family, wrong temperature, or a named color missing (e.g. asked for warm autumn but got greens, or asked for navy but no blue appears). A result that satisfies the request is done; do NOT re-call to make it richer, more vibrant, add variety, or adjust one object. When a second call is warranted, name the exact hues or temperature to correct (e.g. 'warm oranges and reds, not green') and add guideColors for any named color the first call missed \u2014 do not just rephrase. If two calls still conflict with the request, ask the user for clearer direction rather than calling a third time. On failure the error message states the reason and whether a retry is worthwhile \u2014 relay the reason to the user and follow that guidance. A failure the message calls structural won't succeed on the same objects (prefer SetAppearance, or stop); a transient or input failure (e.g. too many UUIDs \u2014 hard cap is 5000, malformed input) is worth one corrected retry. Never call a third time. Fully supported: paths, groups, plugin art (live paint, blends, envelopes), text frames, and symbol instances. Mesh gradients are recolored too, though their palette can be less predictable than flat colors. Applicability depends on the object's actual art type, not how it was created \u2014 a vector-format file imported as native paths/groups is fully supported; check the object's structure rather than assume based on its origin. Skipped (reported in the response): objects with no reachable vector color data \u2014 raster content and opaque placed-item containers \u2014 plus foreign objects, legacy text, graphs, and repeat/symmetry art (radial, grid, symmetry, concentric repeat).

parameters.name: uuids
parameters.description: UUIDs of the vector art objects to recolor. To recolor a whole group, pass the group's UUID, not its children's \u2014 its descendants are recolored with it, so child UUIDs are redundant and waste the 5000-UUID cap. To recolor only some children, pass those children individually; passing the group would recolor its untouched siblings too.

parameters.name: stylePrompt
parameters.description: Theme, mood, or aesthetic description for a Firefly-generated palette. Be specific and concrete \u2014 'deep warm reds and burnt orange, high saturation' yields a closer result than a vague 'more vibrant' or 'warmer'. Hard cap: 500 characters \u2014 stay concise. If you are accreting qualifiers across several refinement turns (e.g. repeated 'X should be more prominent' feedback), rewrite the whole prompt from scratch to state the current target hierarchy tersely rather than appending another clause.

parameters.name: guideColors
parameters.description: Up to 5 anchor colors that influence (but do not guarantee) the generated palette. Whenever the user names specific colors (e.g. 'deep red', 'navy', a hex code), pass them here in addition to stylePrompt \u2014 prose alone anchors the palette less reliably. Accepts: hex like '#RRGGBB' or '#RGB' (sugar), or an object: {\"model\":\"rgb\",\"r\":1,\"g\":0,\"b\":0} | {\"model\":\"cmyk\",\"c\":0,\"m\":1,\"y\":1,\"k\":0} | {\"model\":\"gray\",\"gray\":0.5} | {\"model\":\"swatch\",\"name\":\"PANTONE 185 C\",\"tint\":0.5}. The 'none' sentinel is not accepted here. Per-stop opacity is available via the '#RRGGBBAA' string form or an 'opacity' field (0\u20131) on the object form.

tools.name: SendUserPromptToAIAssistant
tools.description: Asynchronous \u2014 returns immediately after submitting the prompt; the assistant processes it in the background and responses appear in the Illustrator AI Assistant panel, not in this MCP response body. Observe completion via document state changes or AIAgenticSystem logs (correlate with client_query_id). Uses the active document's conversation (via GetConversationIdForDocument). For external MCP clients (e.g. Cursor); not registered with the in-app Illustrator / IRIS agent. Enable the Illustrator feature flag `EnableAIAssistantMCPTool` to expose this tool.

parameters.name: prompt
parameters.description: User message to send to the Illustrator AI Assistant.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: Optional model identifier. Omit to use GetDefaultModel().
